purpose: Subject-level (occupation-level) graduate salary and demand evidence for the Study-to-Career Strategist. Rule #4 of the feature forbids presenting a country average as a subject figure, so only occupation-level sources may populate this. This is a RESEARCH ARTIFACT (raw extracts + provenance), not the validated country corpus: promoting any figure here into corpus requires a reviewed TOPIC_PATHS mapping change plus passing the official-source gate, exactly as the corpus docstring requires. Nothing fabricated; every number carries publisher, source_type, as_of, url and verbatim extract.
basis_convention: All wage figures are GROSS earnings medians (before tax and social insurance) and cover the WHOLE occupation across all experience levels. They are NOT entry-level, NOT degree-specific and NOT take-home. basis: gross. any break-even use would be refused until a net figure with a declared profile exists.

ca-jobbank-lfs-2025-11-19.publisher: Statistics Canada - Labour Force Survey, published by Employment and Social Development Canada via Job Bank
ca-jobbank-lfs-2025-11-19.notes: Median HOURLY wages by NOC. Regional rows for some areas are produced by a Statistics Canada Small Area Estimation model and are therefore ESTIMATE, not OFFICIAL_STATISTICS; only the direct LFS national/provincial rows are recorded as official here.

us-bls-oews-2025-05.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics - Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS)
us-bls-oews-2025-05.notes: Median/mean ANNUAL wages by SOC occupation. Published via the Occupational Outlook Handbook; wage-and-salary employment only (excludes self-employed).

au-jsa-osca-2026-04.publisher: Jobs and Skills Australia - Occupation and Industry Profiles (OSCA), based on ABS data
au-jsa-osca-2026-04.notes: Employment counts and structure. The occupation-specific median weekly earnings are NOT produced for this occupation (the profile states 'median weekly earnings figures are not produced for the following occupations'), so no occupation-level pay figure can be sourced at this granularity - recorded as a gap, not estimated.

claims.statement: In Canada, the median hourly wage for software developers and programmers (NOC 21232) was CAD 48.08 (low CAD 30.29, high CAD 77.40) for reference period 2023-2024, from the Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey.
claims.demand: Labour demand and supply were expected broadly in line over 2024-2033 at the national level (Canadian Occupational Projections System).

claims.statement: In Ontario, the median hourly wage for software engineers and designers (NOC 21231) was CAD 56.73 (low CAD 36.06, high CAD 88.00) for reference period 2023-2024, from the Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey.
In Canada, the median hourly wage for data scientists (NOC 21211) was CAD 46.15 (low CAD 30.00, high CAD 69.74) for reference period 2023-2024, from the Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey.
claims.demand: Labour demand and supply expected broadly in line over 2024-2033.

claims.statement: In Canada, the median hourly wage for civil engineers (NOC 21300) was CAD 48.56 (low CAD 32.00, high CAD 72.12) for reference period 2023-2024, from the Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey.
claims.demand: Employment outlook Moderate for civil engineers (2025-2027).

claims.statement: In the United States, data scientists (SOC 15-2051) had a median annual wage of USD 120,230 (mean USD 126,800; 10th pct USD 67,240; 90th pct USD 199,130) in May 2025, across 262,440 wage-and-salary jobs.
claims.demand: Projected employment growth 35% (2025-2035), about 24,800 openings a year (Occupational Outlook Handbook).

claims.statement: In the United States, civil engineers (SOC 17-2051) had a median annual wage of USD 100,840 (USD 48.48 per hour) in May 2025, across 380,600 jobs; 10th pct under USD 68,240 and 90th pct over USD 163,220.
claims.demand: Employment projected to grow 6% (2025-2035), faster than average; about 22,700 openings per year.

claims.statement: In Australia, 94,900 people were employed as Software Engineers (OSCA 273333) (89.5% full-time), from the Jobs and Skills Australia occupation profile. The occupation-specific median weekly earnings are NOT produced for this occupation.
claims.granularity: occupation-level employment; pay not published at this granularity
claims.reason: Jobs and Skills Australia states median weekly earnings are not produced for this occupation, so no occupation-level pay figure is sourced. This is recorded as not-established rather than estimated, per rule #1/#4. ANSZCO 261313 median weekly earnings were likewise N/A.

coverage_gaps_note: This artifact covers a first tranche (CA x3, US x2, AU x1-with-gap) of the intended country x subject research matrix. Remaining best-covered countries (DE, GB, IE, NL, NZ) and remaining subject/occupation cells are to be harvested in subsequent waves; every cell that cannot be sourced at occupation level must be recorded as a gap with a reason, never filled from a country average.
